text: Ich gebe dem Kind den roten Ball.
why: Phase 1.2: the dative indirect object is obl:arg, not iobj, and used to be dropped entirely because select_object returned the first match. Phrase spans must give 'den roten Ball', not the head token 'Ball'.

text: Lass mich einen Vorschlag machen wie wir zusammen den Nachmittag gestalten.
why: Phase 1.1: the ccomp's subject 'wir' used to be reported against the main clause's verb 'machen'. Roles must resolve per clause.

text: Der Mann, der dort steht, ist mein Vater.
why: Relative clause plus a copular main clause, where the verb is attached as cop.

text: Ich gehe nach Hause und du bleibst hier.
why: Coordination must yield two clauses, and 'nach Hause' a prepositional object.

csubj had to be treated as clause-introducing: 'bist' is the clausal SUBJECT of 'Schön'. Without it 'Du'/'bist' leaked into the main clause and 'Schön' got no role, so no anchor slot existed where an author had in fact placed a command. The verbless predicative clause root is reported as predicate.

Informal greeting. Stanza's charlm default tags 'Hallo' as the root VERB with 'bin' as its ccomp, inventing a second clause; the transformer package the product ships parses it correctly. Promoted from expected-fail once that package became the default, so this is now a plain regression test. A failure here alongside 'Parser package measured: (stanza default)' means the transformer encoder is missing, not that the mapping broke.

text: Schau mal, wie Bob das findet.
why: German imperative. Both the default and the transformer make the adverb 'mal' the sentence root, leaving the main clause verbless; the correct reading is an imperative main clause with verb 'Schau'. Asserts the CORRECT reading.

text: Hey, Ich habe eine Aufgabe für Dich.
why: Regression test for a fixed bug of OURS, not the parser's: select_address's trailing-vocative fallback (written for '..., du Bloedmann!') fired on a leading greeting comma and reported the following subject as the addressee, so 'Ich' was both subject and address. With a greeting comma the addressee sits BEFORE it; a greeting with no name after it has no addressee, and reporting none beats reporting the wrong one.

note: ADJ/ADJD advmod on the participle. The adverbially-used adjective is the whole content of the utterance.
Same shape as de-modverb-01 but Stanza labels it `dep`, not `advmod` — treebank robustness.

text: Das hast Du sehr gut gemacht.
note: Degree adverb nests under the adjective, so both words must be marked. Roles are knownWeak: Stanza assigns Das=nsubj and Du=obj, which is semantically reversed for this fronted-object order.
Verbless predicative fragment: no copula exists, so the predicate has to be taken from the root.
One-word positive feedback. Common in feedback scenes and previously unannotated.
`das` is the subject, not an addressee. The comma fallback used to claim it, and the predicate adjective used to be reported twice — once as predicate, once as a subject modifier.

text: Lass mich einen Vorschlag machen wie wir zusammen weitermachen.
note: Two clauses. The subordinate verb and its adverbial exist only in the clause layer: basic has one verb slot, filled by the main clause. `wie` is SCONJ/KOUS, so it is a linker rather than a modifier.

text: Schau mal, wie Bob das findet.
note: knownWeak for the main clause only: Stanza tags the imperative 'Schau' INTJ and makes the adverb 'mal' the root, so the main clause comes back verbless. The subordinate clause and the linker are asserted as correct.
